transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. Let's get the weekly facilities huddle started. We've got two generators, G-1 and G-2, that cannot be run in parallel, and four operating areas that need power over the next 24 hours: the clinic, communications shelter, cold-storage point, and maintenance workshop. Before I sign off on any generator schedule, I need each of you — medical, signal, facilities, and logistics — to state every changed operating requirement, timing constraint, or circuit-control requirement from your current logs. Let's start with medical. What's changed since last week?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have one changed circuit-control requirement to report. The clinic's vaccine refrigerator was moved to the G-1 circuit during a repair yesterday and must remain on G-1 continuously for the next 24 hours. I confirmed the connection with the clinic technician this morning, but this circuit change is not yet reflected on the facilities drawing.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: Col. Mercer, I have one changed operating requirement and timing constraint to report from the signal side. The communications shelter has a mandatory battery load test scheduled from 1000 to 1100 tomorrow. During that test, the shelter must remain on G-2 throughout — it cannot be switched to G-1 during that window. I received the test notice from the signal maintenance team this morning, but it is not yet on the daily power slide.
